act: Act 4: To Bloom Below the Web

clusters.name: Waking in Willowshore (Spring, Alive at Last)
clusters.scene: After the Act 3 ritual, the PCs awaken near the Eternal Lantern at the south end of Dawnstep Bridge. The world is finely grained and solid - true living reality, no longer a mindscape. The town's state reflects its Act 2 Preparation Points; the town elder thanks the PCs. Over a century has passed, and outsiders who hear of the return will at first fear the PCs are vengeful ghosts.
threads: Reintegrate Willowshore into the living world
clusters.gate: opens Act 4; follows a successful Act 3 transmigration ritual

fragments.plot_point: The Eternal Lantern's item bonus to invoking skill checks increases from +1 to +2 now that the town is among the living.

If the PCs spared the warding bell in Act 3, Karahai gifts it on the PCs' first visit. Installed at any shrine it grants +2 item bonus to all skill checks tied to that deity's divine skill; at a different shrine than the Eternal Lantern's blessing it gives the bonus to two skills.

The roads beyond the hinterlands open: NW Trail to Whisperweb Shrine; Central Northern Road to Moon Marsh; Eastern Northern Road's towns now ghost towns toward the Gossamer Mountains; NE Road's old ranch is now the Silkwasp hideout; Eastern Road to Karahai has the destroyed bridge; Southern 'Apple Road' to the overgrown apple grove.

Silver Collars: a jorogumo's silver collar (non-magical, 50 gp) grants legal right to travel, read/write, and trade outside Shenmen; one should wear it visibly. If missed in Act 3, learned early at Karahai.

The governor's manor returns NE of downtown - but in ruin, overgrown, radiating an aura of being unwelcome. If the PCs don't investigate on their own, the town elder requests it before the first day back alive reaches twilight.

clusters.name: The Governor's Manor: Legality & the Authorization Pass
clusters.scene: Locals believe it illegal under fallen Lung Wa law and the Heavenly Court to enter the manor without a mandate. Custom demands an authorization pass from a sufficiently high government entity. Secretly there are TWO manors: the ruined, monster-filled one explored in Ch.11, and a hidden RESTORED version unlocked later by the Fang and Key.
clusters.gate: town elder grants the pass if they request the investigation; otherwise DC 20 Society to recall the custom

fragments.plot_point: The town elder grants the pass when asking the PCs to investigate. Without it, the lingering power increases the Stealth, Disable, and saving-throw DCs of all manor hazards by 2.

SECRET: there are two manors - the ruined one here is corrupted by Kugaptee; a second, restored manor exists as a hidden mindscape accessible only once the PCs hold the Fang and Key (Ch.13). Withhold.

clusters.name: The Ruined Manor (Ch.11): Hazards, Haunts & Trapped Souls
clusters.scene: The PCs explore the decayed governor's manor (level 10 dungeon) - fine wood/tile/tarnished silver of late Imperial Lung Wa, paper walls gone. Monsters drawn from Kugaptee's will and the spirits of the manor's dead inhabit it; an Unwelcoming Facade haunt repels approachers. Defeating the False Governor cleanses it all instantly.
clusters.gate: approach with the authorization pass for safest entry

fragments.plot_point: Approaching: front door with pass shown is safest. Climb outer walls DC 20 Athletics; flyers enter A2 from above or Squeeze through roof holes DC 25 Acrobatics into A3-A7 (A4's holes need no Squeeze); no holes reach A8.

HAUNT - Unwelcoming Facade (Haunt 10, unique). Stealth DC 32; Disable DC 32 Occultism/Religion to exorcise or DC 35 Society to defer; a legal pass at the front door lowers both by 5. Horrifying Vision: Small+ within 30 ft, DC 29 Will or frightened 1-2 / fleeing / stupefied 1 by degree. Crit success: several spirits infuse the building, only the strongest is evil.

A2 Courtyard (Low 10): Kugaptee's drakauthixes (2), RARE Huge fiend/fungus/nindoru, Creature 9, AC 25, HP 190, weak fire/silver/slashing 10; tentacle +20 reach 30 ft (3d8+6 P + 1d6 mental, Improved Grab); occult innate DC 27 (spirit blast, vision of death, fear). Ambush with 30-ft tendrils from the vines.

A3 Servants' Rooms (Low 10): four people died in their beds; their century-trapped souls rise as Elite Hungry Ghosts (4), Creature 7. A nindoru claw in the wood IDs an akashti (DC 29 Religion) in A8. Treasure: 3 Taljjae tassels; duskwood batsbreath cane. Ghosts rejuvenate unless the manor is cleansed.

A4 Meeting Area: HAZARD Weakened Floor (unique COMPLEX Hazard 11). Stealth +23; Disable DC 33 Crafting x3 or DC 36 Stealth/Nature. Collapse drops the room into toxic mold (DC 34 Reflex or prone); routine 8d6 poison/round (DC 30 basic Fort). Treasure: lumber lord's axe.

A5 Guest Quarters (Low 10): two Senhang (Tianjing) ritual priests died helping Heh's ritual; their corrupted spirits are War Wraiths (2), Creature 9 (robes drift into red butterflies). DC 22 Religion IDs Senhang robes. Treasure: destroyed skyfang crystal (5 gp), moonsilver necklace, burned Tian-Jing incense.
A6 Dining: 12 bottles (10 worth 50 gp each; 1 ascendant dragon spirit; 1 vengeful demon's tears). A7 Storage: six energizing pills (A7b); lacquered waist drum behind shelves (A7c, DC 28 Perception).

A8 Primary Suite (Moderate 10): the room where Heh's ritual backfired and destroyed Willowshore (DC 20 Occultism/Religion; crit = its rushed nature). The only working doors; chanting (a prayer to Kugaptee, in Common) comes from a mass of red butterflies on the ceiling above a kneeling 'Heh Shan-Bao'.

clusters.name: The False Governor (Nindoru Impostor & Manor Climax)
clusters.scene: In A8 the kneeling figure looks exactly like Governor Heh Shan-Bao, alive and well, thanking the PCs and asking to be escorted to the new governor. He is NOT real: an akashti nindoru in a manifested flesh suit. If escorted he tries to kill the town elder and party with an illusory Kugaptee. The tell: this 'Heh' never met the PCs and recalls nothing from Act 3.
clusters.gate: triggered on entering A8 / confronting the kneeling figure

fragments.plot_point: SECRET: the figure is a variant akashti nindoru impersonating Heh Shan-Bao (Deception +29 impersonating). Reveal via his lack of memory of the PCs, or by refusing/attacking. Withhold.

CREATURE - False Governor, RARE Medium fiend/nindoru, Creature 12, AC 32, HP 220, weak silver 15, resist void 15. Occult innate DC 32 (illusory creature, phantasmal calamity, phantom pain, wave of despair). Manifest Body (HP 10 shell; on destruction he emerges, witnesses DC 29 Fort or sickened 2). Stunning Despair (DC 29 Will, stunned 1-3). Soul Shred DC 36. Fights to death.
When the flesh shell is destroyed he uses Stunning Despair; the noise draws any undefeated A3 hungry ghosts and A5 war wraiths to join the fight.

CLEANSE/REWARD: with the False Governor dead, Kugaptee's hold vanishes - Unwelcoming Facade and the A3/A5 undead vanish at once; grant XP even if unfought, plus 80 XP for freeing the souls. Treasure: chamber pot (150 gp), monocle (100 gp), fan of falling words (90 gp case), dragon potion-holder (50 gp) with panaceatic salve, potion of quickness, greater healing potion.
After: the town elder thanks the PCs, lets them keep all manor treasure, and asks them to travel east to Karahai to begin reintegrating Willowshore.

clusters.name: Shinzo's Farewell
clusters.scene: A few days after waking, the shinigami merchant Shinzo arrives one last time to congratulate the PCs and bid farewell; with the town back in the living cycle he must move on. Final chance to buy from his store. He leaves parting gifts.
threads: Reintegrate Willowshore into the living world
clusters.gate: occurs shortly after the PCs awaken in spring

fragments.plot_point: Shinzo won't reveal his true shinigami form in public ('for us, this form is what is truth now'), though he may show it briefly to curious PCs. Last chance to shop his store.
Parting gifts: a phoenix fulu holder plus four fulus - an anathema fulu, a needle thousand-pains fulu, and two greater potency crystals. Then he and Yix fade away.

clusters.name: Rebuilding Karahai Bridge (Reopening Trade)
clusters.scene: Karahai connects Willowshore to Sea of Ghosts trade routes; its bridge was destroyed by mudslides decades ago and Mago Kai's plank patch won't bear heavy loads. Until rebuilt, Willowshore stays cut off. After Shinzo's last visit Karahai (level-3 settlement) is the default item source - orders up to level 11 take a week. The rebuild is the engine of this stretch and triggers the Silkwasp encounter.
clusters.gate: Karahai accessible anytime, but full trade requires the bridge rebuilt

fragments.plot_point: The temporary 5-ft plank bridge is solid (DC 20 Crafting/Engineering Lore). Striding across is safe; any Attack-trait/violent action that crit-fails drops the PC 30 ft into 20-ft water (DC 20 Reflex to Grab the Edge). Climb gorge DC 30 (DC 10 along mudslide); Swim DC 15; lead a Large mount at DC 25 Nature per Stride.

DOWNTIME - Rebuild Karahai Bridge (manipulate): one PC spends 3 days; DC 25 Engineering Lore / DC 27 Crafting / DC 29 Society; others Aid; helpful spellcasters +1 status (to +3). Crit: 1 month. Success: 2 months. Failure (auto if PCs don't engage): 3 months. Crit fail: deaths (1d8), restart at -4. Reward: 120 XP once rebuilt.

clusters.name: Silkwasps at the Bridge (Lo Kuon's Extortion)
clusters.scene: About a week into the rebuild, a messenger reports bandits have seized Karahai Bridge and are extorting the workers - a half dozen with bloodstained neck-bandages, the Silkwasp Bandits. Their charismatic face, Lo Kuon, greets the PCs. This is really a test of resolve and the first move toward war: Lo Kuon and crew are secretly thralls of the jiang-shi Hong Meigui. (Moderate 10.)
clusters.gate: triggers ~1 week after bridge rebuilding begins

fragments.plot_point: Lo Kuon (late 30s) is a real local legend for opposing the jorogumo, but is now inveigled. He plays 'patron of the people' and probes what the PCs know about Kugaptee, feigning ignorance; he won't dissuade them if they think the threat is over.

SECRET: last summer Lo Kuon led the Silkwasps to loot the Tan Sugi Monastery and fell into thrall to Hong Meigui, a jiang-shi agent of Kugaptee. Bloodstained kerchiefs hide a scabbed root-knot throat wound (Kugaptee's symbol); Lo Kuon hides his under his helmet. DC 28 Religion IDs the symbol (auto if seen earlier). Withhold.

Lo Kuon demands 200 gp/month (50 gp if the bridge is finished); haggling halves it regardless of checks (the ruse just feels the PCs out). Pay and they leave; refuse/attack and he draws his shortsword and rolls Deception for initiative.

CREATURES - Lo Kuon (Creature 7, gang leader) + 3 nearby bandits in melee on the loudest speaker; 4 Silkwasp Bandits (Creature 6, monster hunters, longbow + 2 explosive arrows each, +1 greataxe) across the gorge target the BRIDGE (AC 24): 2 hits blow the planks apart, 5 total hits destroy all rebuild work. While inveigled they fight to death.
If captured alive or if the inveigle ritual is dispelled, the bandits instantly surrender; Lo Kuon reveals everything and begs the PCs to come to camp and kill the monster enslaving them.

clusters.name: Dealing with the Bandits (Intel & Escalation)
clusters.scene: If the PCs pay the bridge price the Silkwasps keep escalating - stolen livestock, road robberies, strangers near NE-town buildings - all tests of the town's defenses. Unaddressed, Hong Meigui eventually leads a brazen Extreme assault on the town (no earlier than Ch.13). The PCs can Track them or Gather Information at Karahai.
clusters.gate: ongoing if the PCs don't destroy the Silkwasps

fragments.plot_point: If the PCs paid: trouble recurs every few weeks. If they FOUGHT at the bridge: Hong Meigui speeds up - first reports within days. The longer it festers, the worse the eventual town assault (Extreme, ~Ch.13).

Track to camp DC 20 Survival (after any encounter), or stumble on it exploring. Gather Information at Karahai DC 22 Diplomacy (2 hrs): locals begged the Silkwasps for aid via notes in wasp nests, but no response since early last summer - most assume them dead. Crit fail false lead: their ghosts curse those who pay tribute.

clusters.name: The Silkwasp Camp (Hong Meigui's Lair)
clusters.scene: A ruined farmstead on a bluff over the Sea of Ghosts, ~a day's ride NE. Rickety fences (Climb DC 15), a fishpond, a collapsing barn, a 50-ft cliff (Climb DC 30), boarded windows as arrow slits, a hidden rope (DC 22) to release the cobras. The whole camp is ONE encounter (Severe 10, or Extreme if bridge bandits survived). A rescued Lo Kuon guides the PCs and knows how to put Hong Meigui to rest.
clusters.location: Silkwasp Camp (NE bluff over the Sea of Ghosts)
clusters.gate: PCs locate the camp via a rescued bandit, Tracking, or exploration

fragments.plot_point: A de-inveigled bandit gives directions; only Lo Kuon comes along for revenge and only he knows Hong Meigui is a jiang-shi. His advice: bring handheld mirrors and 1 Bulk glutinous rice or hen eggs to destroy her, and note she keeps a silk-wrapped item she fears/obsesses over in B10.

Layout (one encounter): B1 front gate, B2 storage shack by the pond, B3 inner gate, B4 collapsed granary (cobras), B5/B8 barracks, B6 Lo Kuon's room, B7 pantry, B9 back porch, B10 Hong Meigui's room. Bandits-on-the-Defensive for 1 week after any clash.

CREATURES - Hong Meigui, UNIQUE jiang-shi vampire, Creature 10, AC 29, HP 128 (fast healing 10), +2 striking flaming shock urumi; breathsense (a breath-holder is invisible to her); occult innate DC 29 (charm, paralyze, vampiric feast, hallucination); inveigle ritual; Drain Qi (drained, heals 12). Plus Elite Emperor Cobras (2, Creature 6) and Silkwasp Bandits (5, Creature 6).

Jiang-shi traits: One More Breath (drops to 1 HP at 0; destroy permanently with 1 Bulk glutinous rice/hen eggs while down, or a duskwood/peachwood weapon). Vampiric revulsion to mirrors and ringing handbells. Bitter Epiphany: an altar with 1 Bulk food offerings stupefies her (DC 25 Will). Warped Fulu (brow): immune to item-cast spells; Steal it (vs Perception DC 30), destroy it to end her fast healing.

While she lives, bandits fight to death; once she falls, survivors flee. Treasure (B10 chest, key on her or 3x DC 30 Thievery): 3,500 sp, 220 gp, 120 gp jewelry, vanishing coin talisman, wand of soothe (4th). False bottom (DC 28 Perception): the silk-wrapped JIANG-SHI BELL she fears, in 60-gp spidersilk.

clusters.name: Ren Mei Li Returns (The Silversilk Princess)
clusters.scene: Ch.12. Lady Ren Mei Li, a high-ranking jorogumo whose web includes Willowshore, hears of its return. She has never actually met the PCs (the Act 3 figure was an echo). She returns to 'welcome them below the web' and to learn how Willowshore came back, then sets the Five-Season Treasures missions to test their skill and loyalty. Her official mandate - the Fang and Key - is the only path to ultimately reaching Heh Shan-Bao.
threads: Earn the jorogumo's stewardship / the Fang and Key
clusters.gate: occurs after the PCs reopen contact with the wider world (Karahai/bandits)

fragments.plot_point: SECRET: she wants reliable local stewards so she needn't manage Willowshore, AND secretly to bind the PCs' loyalty to HERSELF over Lady Lang Loi and the court. She'll accept a pact upholding only her interests, even leaving the PCs free to work against jorogumo rule. Frame her as someone to WORK WITH, not an enemy.

SECRET: only the jorogumo court's official mandate - the ceremonial Fang and Key - lets the PCs finally defeat Heh Shan-Bao and prevent Kugaptee's reincarnation. PCs can technically complete Ch.12 without it but miss major content.

clusters.name: A Feline Emissary (Amai the Dweomercat)
clusters.scene: A week before her arrival, Ren Mei Li sends her loyal dweomercat Amai to announce the visit. Amai (sapphire fur, violet spirals, elegant silver-spidersilk collar) watches the townsfolk and PCs from hiding (DC 27 Perception). Unusually devoted for a dweomercat, she gossips fondly about her mistress - a clue this jorogumo is powerful enough to earn loyalty from a fickle being. (Trivial 11.)
threads: Earn the jorogumo's stewardship / the Fang and Key
clusters.gate: appears a week ahead of Ren Mei Li's visit

fragments.plot_point: Amai invites the PCs to tea with Ren Mei Li in 7 days; she answers a few questions (asking a guileless one back each time) then leaves after ~5 minutes. If the PCs befriended the teahouse bakeneko Yami, Yami can meet and befriend Amai first.
No real option to refuse the visit. Attacking Amai makes her flee, and Ren Mei Li thereafter treats the PCs as criminals working off a debt rather than allies. Reward: 40 XP for speaking with her.

Preparing (a full week, no checks): receive her at the Cerulean Teahouse. Gather Information at Karahai or from a surviving bandit (DC 25): she's a 'less harrowing' jorogumo, accepts tengu, rarely demands people, reacts well to arcana (crit). Wear silver collars. Reward 40 XP.

clusters.name: Meeting the Princess (The Tea Audience)
clusters.scene: At the appointed hour Ren Mei Li arrives in silver mist - a silver-haired beauty in blue-green silk, jeweled-spider hair sticks (living spiders), silver-sheen eyes. She appears alone in human shape to seem less intimidating, and offers an alliance: protection from Sze's greed and considerable autonomy, if its stewards are people she can trust. Over tea she probes how the PCs brought the town back.
threads: Earn the jorogumo's stewardship / the Fang and Key
clusters.gate: occurs 7 days after Amai's invitation, if the PCs are receptive

fragments.plot_point: Her start attitude is indifferent; visibly wearing the Act 3 silver collars shifts it to friendly. Impress her over the meal: DC 28 Diplomacy/Performance/Society/Tea Lore or DC 23 Arcana for Victory Points. 3+ VP improves her attitude one step (friendly, or helpful if already friendly).

She asks incisive questions about the mindscape, the Kugaptee clashes, and the PCs' civic work; inventive tactics and concrete achievements impress her. She promises nothing specific but hints at a Silver Seal village 'with a trustworthy steward.'

clusters.name: The Princess's Requests (Five-Season Treasures)
clusters.scene: Tradition demands new stewards complete a loyalty/competence ritual: the Five-Season Treasures. Four symbolize the seasons of life (spring's bright bird, summer's fiery flowers, autumn's sweet fruits, winter's spiced tea); the fifth - beyond mortal life - offers the gifts to the honored dead for the ancestors' blessing. Then the PCs swear fealty and the stewardship is theirs. Each rite yields up to 4 Victory Points. She asks fealty to HERSELF.
threads: Earn the jorogumo's stewardship / the Fang and Key
clusters.gate: offered after the PCs accept (tentatively) the stewardship discussion

fragments.plot_point: She asks for personal fealty 'to me' rather than to Lady Lang Loi or the court; if challenged she shrugs, 'Oh, was that what I said?' Withhold the significance until the PCs grasp her self-interest.
Each of the five rites grants up to 4 Victory Points (max 20). The cumulative VP determines Ren Mei Li's final reward. Reward: 60 XP for agreeing to pursue her requests.

SECRET - Treasure AND Murder: while the PCs chase the treasures, the real Heh Shan-Bao (now a yohoi) sneaks into town to MURDER townsfolk and spread terror. Killings happen while the PCs are out; they investigate the scenes between rites. Withhold the killer's identity.

What's a Yohoi? (learned via the murders): DC 20 Occultism/Society/Willowshore Lore or Gather Information reveals one fact (two on crit): they prey on rural towns, once thought neglected-ancestor ghosts, now a boogeyman; bulging yellow eyes, crooked hairy necks, long filthy nails; kill via mental anguish; fear holy flute music; a dead yohoi fades in minutes and can return unless slain finally; they're 'brainchildren' of a community's fears. Reward: 80 XP once a yohoi is suspected.

clusters.name: Event 1: Bright Spring Bird (The Show)
clusters.scene: The first treasure is a theatrical performance evoking brightness and optimism about the new rule, celebrating the PCs' greatest deed (freeing the town from the mindscape). A chance to develop NPCs' reactions to lurching a century forward. Staged at the Seven-Colored Songbird theater (introducing director Kazuma Oono before his later fate). Ren Mei Li arrives in silver mist to watch.
clusters.gate: first of the five rites; ~1 week to prepare

fragments.plot_point: Putting on the show: each PC describes their contribution and rolls DC 28 with an apt skill for Victory Points - Performance, Crafting (sets/costumes), Arcana/Nature/Occultism/Religion (effects), Acrobatics/Athletics (stunts), or Deception/Diplomacy/Intimidation (hosting Ren Mei Li).

NPC color: lawyer Luo Xi Yang frets her Lung Wa legal expertise is useless under jorogumo codes; inventor Huo Tian-Zhe is annoyed his clockwork is now 'charming antiques'; trader Kim Gu-won mourns dead partners but is excited by new trade samples.

After: Ren Mei Li congratulates everyone, gives the bird cloisonne ball to the highest roller, and assigns Event 2 (Fiery Flowers of Summer) - fireworks from dried Hei Feng's horn blossoms in Moon Marsh. Reward: 80 XP for 1+ VP, 120 XP for max 4 VP.

clusters.name: Event 2: Fiery Flower Fireworks (Moon Marsh & Isori)
clusters.scene: The summer treasure: a real fireworks display colored fiery orange by fresh petals of Hei Feng's horn, a night-blooming wetland flower abundant in Moon Marsh (~18 miles north). The grove is decorated with astrolabes, sundials, lenses, and glass beads hung by Isori, a reclusive awakener naga astrologer who has detected Kugaptee's 'creeping chains' reaching into nature. He isn't naturally violent.
clusters.gate: assigned after Event 1; ~1 week

fragments.plot_point: Finding flowers: 8 hrs daylight search or 1 hr after dark (they glow at night). CREATURE - Isori, awakener naga, Creature 6, Perception +22, has breath of life. If attacked he offers a truce each round, avoids killing PCs (even revives the fallen), flees below 75 HP. If not attacked, introduces himself as 'guardian of this swamp.'

Isori has sensed Kugaptee's encroaching corruption ('creeping chains') and wonders if the PCs caused it. Make an Impression DC 27: friendly = one thousand-year dragonroot; helpful = all three (else found at DC 30 Perception, 1 hr Search).

Harvest petals: secret DC 28 Crafting/Herbalism Lore/Nature/Survival (others Aid DC 20). Crit = +2 circ to later firework checks; failure -2 (-4 crit fail). Friendly+ Isori lowers harvest DCs by 4. Then craft & launch fireworks (DC 28 Crafting / Arcana/Nature/Occultism/Religion / Performance for VP).

After: Ren Mei Li gives the fireworks ball and assigns Event 3 (Sweet Fruits of Autumn) - an apple grove south now home to 'something disagreeable.' Reward: 60 XP for 1+ VP / 80 XP max; +40 XP if Isori made friendly+.

clusters.name: Event 3: Fall's Sweet Fruits (The Overgrown Apple Grove)
clusters.scene: The autumn treasure: restore a beloved apple grove ~20 miles south, now overgrown and, for seven years, the lair of monsters - elephant-sized trails littered with crunched giant-spider remains. (Moderate 11.) Apple season is months away, but starting the restoration satisfies the rite.
clusters.gate: assigned after Event 2; ~1 week to begin the work

fragments.plot_point: CREATURES - Khravgodons (4), Creature 9 (huge spider-eating opossums), ambush with Stealth initiative; one below 40 HP flees but returns. If communication is possible the PCs might broker a relocation; otherwise all four must be slain before restoration.
Treasure (auto once restoration starts, or 1 hr Search): a long-dead adventurer's skeleton in dragon turtle armor with a dragon turtle artillery cylinder.

Restoring the grove (planning suffices): each PC rolls DC 28 for VP - Nature, Arcana/Occultism/Religion (magic), Diplomacy (recruit workers), Farming Lore (prune/weed), Survival (protective traps). Reward: 60 XP for 1+ VP / 80 XP max. The FIRST murder occurs while the PCs are here.

clusters.name: The Murders Begin (Investigation Framework)
clusters.scene: Three murders occur during Ch.12 (GM may add more). Each leaves a crime scene plus event-specific leads; all three bodies share clues: emaciated frames, missing eyes, strange wrist runes. The killer is the real Heh Shan-Bao, now a yohoi, who portals from the corrupted mindscape into his ruined manor, translocates to lone targets, and flees - leaving no trail. Investigation uses the Search for Clues activity.
elements: emaciated bodies / missing eyes / wrist runes
the portal in the ruined manor
clusters.gate: runs in parallel with the Five-Season Treasures rites

fragments.plot_point: SECRET: the murderer is Heh Shan-Bao himself, transformed into a yohoi ruling the corrupted mindscape. He emerges by night via a portal in the ruined manor (unknown to the PCs until they hold the Fang and Key) and translocates to visited targets. Yohoi stats p.354. Withhold his identity.

ACTIVITY - Search for Clues (concentrate/exploration/secret): 10 min Investigating a body/evidence/scene OR 2 hrs Gathering Information; then roll the scene's check. Crit = minor+moderate+major; Success = minor+moderate; Failure = minor; Crit fail = a false lead believed true. Investigators can Pursue a Lead / Clue In.

Shared body clues (investigable across all three): emaciated frames, missing eyes, strange wrist runes (later seen as spectral shackles in Kugaptee's Grasp). Four more shared investigations + the yohoi stats are on p.354-355.

Speaking to the Dead (if available): corpses describe the killer's rootlike body, butterflies from his eyes, long broken arms - and can ID him as a distorted Heh Shan-Bao. Staking out the manor at night may let PCs confront the yohoi early (Moderate 11; slaying him reforms him in the mindscape, but he won't murder in town again). 80 XP per murder prevented.

clusters.name: Event 4: The First Murder (Kazuma Oono)
clusters.scene: While the PCs are at the apple grove, Heh Shan-Bao kills Kazuma Oono, the Songbird theater director - bitter over Oono's handling of 'The Chronicle of the Water-Weaver' and afraid Oono could help the PCs. Oono is killed at his desk, notebook stolen. Found in his locked office (lock undisturbed) with a paper wall smashed outward from within, bloody smears, no struggle.
elements: missing play 'The Chronicle of the Water-Weaver'
clusters.gate: occurs during/after Event 3 (the apple grove)

fragments.plot_point: SCENE - Search for Clues DC 25 Perception. Minor: killer entered calmly, exited by smashing the paper doorway, no outside tracks. Moderate: a blood-handprinted trunk of annotated plays; DC 25 Theater/Willowshore Lore shows one missing - The Chronicle of the Water-Weaver. Major: auto-realize it's missing AND find a draft of 'The Endless Shore' (a significant personal token to free Oono in Ch.13). False lead: anti-Southbank politics.

THE CHRONICLE OF THE WATER-WEAVER - Search for Clues DC 22 Willowshore Lore. A play about a monk who weaves cloth from water amid silk-trader intrigue over a fickle governor. Major: Oono was reworking it as a blatant critique of Governor Heh Shan-Bao; the governor visited him at end of spring (before his ritual) and all talk of the production went silent. False lead: it was simply out of rotation.

INTERVIEWS - Gather Information DC 22 Diplomacy. Minor: Oono last seen at dusk soaking at the Happy Kappa bathhouse with Hua De-ge, in good spirits. Moderate: excited about a new play from the PCs' Spring Bird show, heading to the theater to write. Major: weeks before the last day of spring, Governor Heh visited; a heated argument was heard, leaving Oono depressed. Reward: 80 XP for first linking the crimes to Heh Shan-Bao or finding a personal token.

clusters.name: Event 5: Spiced Tea of Winter (Whisperweb Shrine & the Algrievers)
clusters.scene: The winter treasure: spiced tea strained through the finest silk from the algrievers of Whisperweb Shrine to the NW. The idyllic clearing holds a beautiful pond, stacked-stone shrines, and tree-hung ornaments - lanterns, gilt masks, woven silk, and the silk-wrapped mummified corpses of animals and people. The six algrievers (spider-like spirit custodians, NOT evil) won't let the PCs leave until they honor the forgotten goddess Daikitsu. (Severe 10 if it comes to battle.)
clusters.gate: assigned after Event 3; ~1 week

fragments.plot_point: The algrievers (Creature 9, x6) emerge atop the rock shrines and challenge the intruders, demanding the PCs perform rites to 'those you have forgotten' - a tea ceremony for Daikitsu. If attacked or if silk is taken, they hiss and fight to the death but seek to TRAP the PCs alive (not kill) so they can repent.

Honoring the Shrine: each PC rolls DC 28 for VP - Religion/Tea Lore, Diplomacy (cooperation), Performance (supplement), Arcana/Nature/Occultism (magic). Volunteering unprompted = +2 circ; being captured and forced = -2. Even 0 VP, if the algrievers believe the PCs tried, lets them harvest silk and leave in peace.

If the PCs earn 3+ VP, the algrievers grant up to 6 willing PCs a Pilgrim's Ward (kept while obeying Daikitsu's edicts/anathema). Killing them eases silk-gathering but forfeits VP. Reward: 60 XP for 1+ VP / 80 XP max; full combat XP if resolved without violence.

clusters.name: Event 6: The Second Murder (Elizeth Candora)
clusters.scene: Heh Shan-Bao's second victim is Elizeth Candora, caretaker of Her Fluvial Lady of Souls (Pharasma's temple) - targeted for her Pharasmin ties and his yohoi terror of flute music. Killed as she plays flute over the graveyard, draped over Oono's fresh grave. Found after the PCs return from Whisperweb. The town goes on high alert: a sundown curfew and a -1 circumstance penalty to Earn Income / Gather Information in Willowshore.
clusters.location: Willowshore (Her Fluvial Lady of Souls / graveyard)
clusters.gate: occurs after the PCs return from Event 5 (Whisperweb)

fragments.plot_point: SCENE - Search for Clues DC 25 Perception. Minor: her broken flute lies by Oono's grave; DC 25 Perception shows it broke from SONIC, not impact (DC 20 Identify Magic = shatter spell). The broken flute is a significant personal token to free Elizeth in Ch.13. Moderate: she played over fresh graves to guide souls - breaking the flute suggests cruelty aimed at Oono's soul; auto-confirm shatter. Major: the broken flute points to a YOHOI (they fear holy flute music). False lead: a jilted-lover theory.
Reward: 60 XP for discovering Elizeth's broken flute. The curfew/fear penalty persists until the killer is dealt with.

clusters.name: Event 7: The Final Season (Walking the Gossamer Path)
clusters.scene: Ren Mei Li returns, now letting her eight spider legs unfurl. She lays out the real bargain: stewardship and a Silver Seal's autonomy for an oath of PERSONAL fealty to her, superseding loyalty to Lady Lang Loi and the court, kept discreet. If the PCs agree (or convincingly Lie, DC 39 Deception), she sends them to walk the Gossamer Path and seek the veiled path maidens for counsel on the murders. She gives a gossamer sash and sanctified beans.
threads: Earn the jorogumo's stewardship / the Fang and Key
clusters.gate: occurs after Events 5/6; the sash reaches the path maidens without the long journey

fragments.plot_point: Her offer: personal fealty to HER over the court; outwardly the PCs play loyal subjects, ask her to intercede against unreasonable jorogumo demands, and she promises protection. If they REJECT: no sash/beans, just a scroll of sending to recall her later; she warns them not to make her an enemy.
Gifts on acceptance: a gossamer sash (contact path maidens from any road after midnight, no travel needed) and 4 sanctified beans (aid if the meeting goes poorly).

Walking the Gossamer Path (Low 11): after an hour walking a night road, the sash drops up to 4 PCs into a 10-ft mountain-path mindscape. A path maiden (Creature 12) appears; via the sash she parleys, else attacks. The PCs get ONE chance to answer (each PC DC 34 Diplomacy; need 1 success, no crit fail) and ONE question. Her knowledge covers the dead in Shenmen, including the recently-returned-to-life.

REVELATION - the right question (Kugaptee, Heh Shan-Bao, or the murders): the maiden steps aside and a silver mirror shows the RESTORED manor, zooming to a fanged-fiend-locked cypress door (not in the PCs' prior visits) in the primary suite. The lock's face becomes Heh Shan-Bao's, reciting 'Greed and shame... A man becomes a monster... only a rightful ruler shall carry the key to my domain!' - naming the killer and the Fang-and-Key path. Withhold until earned.

clusters.name: Event 8: The Third Murder (You So-Jin)
clusters.scene: Heh Shan-Bao's third victim is grave keeper-alchemist You So-Jin (Graveside Manners), killed because he senses her new anti-nindoru bomb research. This occurs after the Gossamer Path but before Ren Mei Li's last visit. Her shop is wrecked - destroyed stock, a smashed lab - and her body is in the same grisly condition. Found late morning after curfew lifts.
clusters.gate: occurs after Event 7 (Gossamer Path)

fragments.plot_point: SCENE - Search for Clues DC 27 Perception. Minor: the killer lingered, fighting or ransacking (unlike the first two). Moderate: she died as fast as the others - the wreckage was a frenzied search/rage; 10 more min Searching the lab (DC 27) finds an old FAMILY JOURNAL behind a dresser atop a metal case (a significant personal token to free So-Jin in Ch.13). Major: auto-find journal AND silversoul bombs. False lead: her herbalism gave protection.

Treasure: the journal holds a RARE silversoul bomb formula (anti-nindoru) she'd just completed - she'd meant to gift it and the bombs to the PCs. The metal case holds 3 silversoul bombs + 500 gp of powdered silver/supplies (+2 item to craft more). Reward: 80 XP. If her murder was PREVENTED, she gifts the bombs/formula at the start of Ch.13.

clusters.name: The Fang and Key (Stewardship Granted)
clusters.scene: A week after the Gossamer Path, Ren Mei Li returns, hears the PCs' report (undeterred if they didn't ask the right question), then produces a large golden key with four hollows and dangling spider fangs. The four Five-Season cloisonne balls lock into its shaft and it glows. She asks the PCs to swear themselves as Willowshore's stewards; accepting the key makes it official.
threads: Earn the jorogumo's stewardship / the Fang and Key
clusters.gate: granted ~1 week after the Gossamer Path

fragments.plot_point: The Fang and Key is ceremonial - its only intrinsic power is acting as an everlight crystal. Its REAL purpose: while a PC carries it, Heh Shan-Bao's domain welcomes them as legal rulers, letting them enter the restored manor and use its mindscape door into the corrupted mindscape (Ch.13). Withhold this function until Ch.13.

VP rewards: 10+ VP across the five rites earns a type II spacious pouch (spidersilk) holding evil-reflecting shield, fortune cord, purgatory emissary's staff, sensei's parasol - choose ONE. Each VP above 10 = one more item; 14+ VP = all four plus the bag. Reward: 80 XP for becoming stewards and gaining the Fang and Key.

clusters.name: Bonus: The Un-Weavers (Quintessivore Bargain)
clusters.scene: An optional bonus encounter (the act needn't end on the last day of the season). Willowshore's strange return attracts other fiends. Four quintessivores - the self-styled 'Un-Weavers,' spider-like soul-feeders - manifest near the PCs (taken for the town's leaders) and propose an unsettling deal rather than fight blind. (Severe 11.)
clusters.gate: optional; use for extra XP/gear or pacing

fragments.plot_point: Their offer: surrender one Willowshore 'fresh soul' now and one on the first day of every following season, and the Un-Weavers protect the town from other predators (they likely won't honor it). Agreeing wrecks the PCs' reputation and may draw Ren Mei Li's confrontation. Refusing triggers an attack (Deception/Diplomacy/Intimidation for initiative).

CREATURES - Quintessivores (4), RARE Medium beast, Creature 10, AC 28, HP 180; blade-leg +22 (1d10+9 S + 1d10 void + tattered soul/drained); arcane prepared DC 29 (grim tendrils, fly, vision of death, vampiric feast); Instant Suspension + Suspend Soul (stalls a dying creature, DC 29 Will); Feed on Quintessence makes resurrecting a fed-upon soul require DC 31 Religion/Occultism. Tattered Soul DC 29 Fort or drained.

clusters.name: A Fiend in Two Worlds (Ch.13 Opens / The Restored Manor)
clusters.scene: With the murder clues and the mirror riddle, the PCs realize the killer is Heh Shan-Bao - or something wearing his face - and that as stewards they can use the Fang and Key to reach him. Approaching within 30 ft of the ruined manor, a steward PC sees it transform into a fully RESTORED manor lit by unsettling red light. If the PCs lag, Ren Mei Li can nudge them.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: requires the PCs to be made stewards (carry the Fang and Key) and to approach the manor

fragments.plot_point: SECRET: Heh Shan-Bao restored the manor as a mindscape to seal off intruders from the corrupted mindscape where he rules - he didn't anticipate a jorogumo making the PCs legal rulers. Only stewards (and the installed town elder, once official) can see/enter the restored manor. Withhold.

Manor Features: a PC can concentrate 1 round outside to 'shift focus' between the ruin and the restored version, but once inside the restored manor they can't switch. DC 25 Arcana/Occultism confirms it's a mindscape, enterable at will by Willowshore's rightful rulers. Anyone in contact with a steward when they cross travels too; otherwise they can't enter or, if abandoned inside, can't leave. Only the front doors at C1 cross between worlds.

clusters.name: The Restored Manor (Ch.13 Dungeon & Links to Heh's Past)
clusters.scene: The restored manor (level 12) is a mindscape lit by red lanterns of writhing nindoru butterflies; silver accents stripped away. It holds jiang-shi guardians, a cursed safe, an occult living rune, a curse-eating fey, and four personal LINKS to Heh Shan-Bao's human life that protect the PCs in the mindscape and can free him in the finale. The northern bedroom door is the mindscape door into Kugaptee's Grasp.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
elements: Wisdom of the Seven Sages + letter
clusters.gate: enterable once the PCs are stewards; the Fang and Key unlocks the safe and the mindscape door

fragments.plot_point: C1 Entrance: two crimson-eyed stone lions salute the PCs (not dangerous); entering noisily alerts the C3a jiang-shi. C2 Courtyard: koi pool, eternal clear-night sky (barrier at 15 ft). One scroll is torn apart - Princess Ok Jinju of Hwanggot (DC 30 Society IDs her), Heh's impossible university love; he couldn't bear to damage her face. The PORTRAIT SCRAP is a link to free Heh (5 gp).

C3 Servants' Quarters (Low 12): two jiang-shi (Creature 11, UNIQUE; Hong Meigui's traits - One More Breath, breathsense, Warped Fulu, Bitter Epiphany) endlessly re-sort documents in C3a; they demand the PCs leave, then attack and fight to death.

C4 Meeting Area: a lion-faced safe (4x DC 30 Thievery, or the Fang and Key auto-unlocks). HAZARD Witherweird Runes (RARE magical trap, Hazard 13): Stealth DC 37; Disable DC 37 Device / DC 40 Arcana / dispel 7th (DC 31). Withering Wail when a non-Heh opens the hidden compartment: DC 33 Fort, up to 30d6 void + clumsy/enfeebled curse, alerting C3a/C6 jiang-shi.

C4 Treasure & Lore: shelves hold 'The Wisdom of the Seven Sages' (Heh's graduation gift from his father) with a folded LETTER from his proud parents - both LINKS to free Heh. Safe: 10x 100 gp; hidden compartment ledgers prove Heh illegally sold lumber for personal luxury, bought an occult living rune to guard 'wartime collectibles' in C7c, plus a smudged 'deactivation mantra' for the rune.

C5 Guest Quarters: the Tianjing priests stayed here (the A5 war wraiths). Treasure: an intact skyfang crystal (lets the PCs Track spirits in the Grasp); a meditation mandala (countering charm w/ warp mind) to free the corrupted monks later. C6 Dining (Moderate 12): three jiang-shi (Creature 11), melancholic, stupefied 2 for 1 min at combat start; fight to death.

C7 Storage (Low 12): C7c guarded by an OCCULT LIVING RUNE (Creature 13, AC 34, HP 245, truesight, wrathful blast +25 4d12 mental, occult innate DC 35). The smudged mantra (from C4) can deactivate it (2-action DC 37 Occultism; crit success destroys, crit fail makes it immune). Treasure: dragonfire halfbow, four-tiger blade, thundering fury dadao.

C8 Master Bedroom (Trivial 12): the cypress mindscape DOOR (fanged-fiend gold lock) into Kugaptee's Grasp - the Fang and Key unlocks it for 1 min. Guarded by ITHINIAK, a curse-eating imprecasia fey (Creature 11) sniffing the lock, trapped here; more willing to talk than fight. He removes curses for being led out but uses Devour Curse (may drain) unless made friendly+.

C8 Treasure & final LINKS: Heh's private DIARY (his fear, his excuse 'all pay some, and none pays all'), and a preserved pink CAMELLIA FLOWER wrapped in a gold ribbon reading 'Summer's virtues never fade' (Princess Adavisha's Lament; DC 30 Society/Academia Lore). The flower & ribbon are the fourth LINK to free Heh.

clusters.name: Kugaptee's Grasp (The Corrupted 'What-If' Willowshore)
clusters.scene: Through the C8 door lies the corrupted mindscape - 'Kugaptee's Grasp,' a sprawling nightmare city under a sky of boiled blood, sunless, spangled with glowing eyes, dominated by a colossal clawed arm where the Great Willow stood. Heh Shan-Bao ruled here 115 'real-time' years as Kugaptee's vessel, growing the town into a city of undead and fiends from Kugaptee's dead dreams. The PCs arrive shackled by spectral chains and must explore, free the murdered souls, and reach the claw.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: requires passing through the C8 mindscape door with the Fang and Key

fragments.plot_point: SECRET (deep backstory): after the PCs escaped, Kugaptee's redirected corruption flooded the vacuum and drew Heh Shan-Bao in via his shame/guilt; he waited out 115 years as the Grasp grew from town to monster-city. He needs only to gather living souls (the 3 murders are the minimum), ripen them, then give himself to Kugaptee so the nindoru reincarnates and topples the Tan Sugi. Not on a strict timer, but dawdling = more murders. Withhold.

On arrival each PC's wrists gain spectral shackle runes (matching the victims'). DC 30 Identify Magic: while in the Grasp the PCs are doomed 1 (can't drop below 1); crit = if you die here Kugaptee claims your soul (resurrection/animation counteracted +23, rank 7). ESCAPE: defeat Heh Shan-Bao (all fade), or simply CARRY one of the four links to his past - worn or in a carried container.
The mindscape door persists in the arrival plaza and, once Fang-and-Key-unlocked, stays unlocked for the PCs thereafter - their route back to the restored manor and the living world.

Grasp Features: faceless phantom townsfolk shuffle (mere figments); buildings are 2D, empty, with illegible writing; shops bear placards 'ALL GOODS TO BE SENT TO THE MOST GLORIOUS GOVERNOR'S GRASP'; homes hold only basket-headed wicker effigies - even mock effigies of the PCs at the Cerulean Teahouse, faces painted as childish Heh Shan-Baos. Optional tableaux: The Lumber Scales, The Peddler of Glories (DC 25 Society), The Puppet Mother - chanting from dead red butterflies.

clusters.name: The Chained Spirits (Freeing the Murdered Souls)
clusters.scene: The souls Heh Shan-Bao murdered are pulled into the Grasp, bound as weeping shades near where they died. Ironically, by murdering each out of fear, he gave each a weapon the PCs can use - but only by RELEASING them via the Free Shackled Soul activity (using its murder-scene token gives +3). Each freed soul grants a lasting +2 status save bonus and weakens Heh in the finale; a murder prevented in Ch.12 grants the benefit automatically.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: each requires reaching the soul's death-site within the Grasp (skyfang crystal can Track them)

fragments.plot_point: ACTIVITY - Free Shackled Soul (auditory/concentrate/exploration/linguistic/mental): speak 10 min; DC 28 soul-specific skill OR DC 32 Diplomacy/Intimidation; carrying the soul's token = +3 item. Crit = freed AND resurrected (7th-rank resurrect, returns to life); Success = freed, moves to the Boneyard (stays dead); Failure = retry; Crit fail = sinks deeper, freeable only when Heh is defeated.

Oono (Songbird Theater, ~200 ft SW; DC 30 Perception, +4 with Fang and Key) endlessly revises 'The Chronicle of the Water-Weaver.' Free via DC 28 Deception (subtler satire) or the standard checks. Reward: the play returns to the real world and grants the party +2 status to WILL saves for the rest of the adventure; 80 XP.

Elizeth (graveyard behind the ruined Pharasmin cathedral) drags buried chains, repairing a falling-apart flute over defiled graves. Free via DC 28 Performance or the standard checks. Reward: +2 status to REFLEX saves for the rest of the adventure; 80 XP.

You So-Jin (her shop, chained to her bench) keeps failing to craft a stronger silversoul bomb (harmless explosions). Free via DC 28 Crafting or the standard checks. Reward: +2 status to FORTITUDE saves for the rest of the adventure; 80 XP. A murder PREVENTED in Ch.12 grants that soul's bonus + finale benefit automatically.

clusters.name: Kugaptee's Grave (Four Memory Battles)
clusters.scene: Once all three souls are freed (or the PCs approach the claw), the streets of the Grasp narrow into a cavern-like maze - Kugaptee's Grave. Four doors at alley-ends open onto warped recreations of the PCs' past adventures (one per season), each a combat evoking a prior act. The path ends at the door to Heh Shan-Bao's manor and the final encounter.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: entered when approaching the claw or after freeing the third soul

fragments.plot_point: D1 Summertime Guard (Moderate 12): a recreated Dawnstep Bridge. GURGLEGUT, UNIQUE buso, Creature 12 (13 ft, +1 flaming crossbow, Spit Fire 10d8, Command Onidoshi) with 4 Mountain Oni (Creature 8). Spared (made indifferent fast / shown mercy), he shrinks to his Act-1 self, gives his gear, warns 'the playthings of Kugaptee enjoy using the dead as disguises!' then Kugaptee kills him (head bursts into red butterflies).

D2 A Fallen Tree (Moderate 12): the Tan Sugi courtyard with a dead tree. DC 38 Perception spots a CORPSE SUGI (UNCOMMON corpseroot, Creature 12, AC 32, HP 242, axe vulnerability, Thoughtblight aura, Take Root drain) bearing Xin Yue's hateful face, plus 4 KAGEKUMAS (Creature 8 nindoru). If undetected, the falling tree hits a 40-ft cone (8d6, DC 27 Reflex). All fight to death.

D3 Lord of Winter (Moderate 12): a recreated Karahai courtyard in freezing rain (DC 27 Fort or enfeebled). 'Mago Kai' (an ARGYREI nindoru, Creature 13, illusory-disguised headless silver-sword monster) and his 'servant' (an AKASHTI, Creature 10, disguised as a dead ally). They offer cursed silver teacups (infected silver curse) and lure the PCs onward; if attacked, reveal true forms. Slain argyrzei becomes a +2 greater striking silver weapon (infected silver curse, DC 33 Will).

D4 Spring's Path (Moderate 12): the Gossamer Path ledge (100-ft drop, DC 25 Reflex to Grab the Edge). Two PATH MAIDENS (Creature 12), Kugaptee's creations (red butterflies, Blasphemous Aura + Corrupting Doubt) order the PCs back and attack. The north wooden door is Heh Shan-Bao's manor door.

clusters.name: The Governor's Den (Entering the Final Manor)
clusters.scene: The D4 north doors open into a haze resolving to C1 of the governor's manor - but at the heart of Kugaptee's influence. The walls are covered with hundreds of darting red eyes (Perception +26); if they spot the PCs, Heh Shan-Bao (waiting in the courtyard) is alerted. Areas appear as C3-C8 but empty of creatures/hazards/treasure. Opening any door into the courtyard triggers the final encounter.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
elements: the southern door back to the Grasp
clusters.gate: reached after the four Kugaptee's Grave chambers

fragments.plot_point: The PCs can retreat south to the Grasp (re-entering via the ruined manor, requiring another trip through the Grave to return), or push into the courtyard. Opening any courtyard door triggers Below Kugaptee's Claw.

clusters.name: Below Kugaptee's Claw (The Final Battlefield)
clusters.scene: The courtyard is a nightmare - a blood pool, a bone fountain, diseased foliage, lanterns of skinned faces, a red-eye moon, the colossal claw cradling it. A blood-rooted wood burl (Kugaptee's heart) sits north; for each soul still shackled, a pair of impaled eyes stares from its roots. Familiar-looking corpses of beloved NPCs lie strewn about - some are disguised shisagishin nindorus, scaling to how many souls the PCs freed. (Varies 12.)
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: triggered by opening a courtyard door in the final manor

fragments.plot_point: CREATURES - SHISAGISHINS (Creature 12) disguised among the corpses, scaling to freed souls: 0 freed = 4 (Extreme 12); 1 freed = 3 (Severe 12); all 3 freed = 2 (Moderate 12). Touching a Corpse Shell triggers Burst From Death; otherwise they rise after 1 min. They fight to death. Freeing souls directly weakens this fight.

The wood burl is a manifestation of Kugaptee's heart; if all souls are freed its roots are merely bloodstained, otherwise a pair of impaled eyes per shackled soul. The corpse disguises echo Gurglegut's warning about the dead being used as disguises.

clusters.name: Heh Shan-Bao Arrives (Free Him or Fight Him)
clusters.scene: When the last shisagishin falls, the claw twitches and a door opens: Heh Shan-Bao the yohoi enters flanked by two crawling parodies of himself - 'Unlived Lives' (unrisen) for the governor and scholar he might have been. Calm if no eyes were lost, furious if souls were freed. The PCs can FREE him via Influence (the four life-links grant more rounds) or fight - both can stop Kugaptee's return.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: triggered when the last shisagishin is defeated

fragments.plot_point: CREATURES - HEH SHAN-BAO (UNIQUE nascent vessel for Kugaptee, Creature 13, yohoi; stats p.354), plus two UNLIVED LIVES (unrisen, Creature 11). Heh hangs back casting innate spells, then claws; uses Steal Soul on a viable target (once). He doesn't start combat unless the PCs leave/attack or negotiations fail.

Released-souls effects (each freed soul weakens him): unrisen lose 20 HP on Rising Again per soul (40 HP if all three). 1 soul = Heh loses frightful presence; 2 = also loses Strike slashing damage; 3 = also loses his physical-damage resistance.

INFLUENCE - Speaking with Heh Shan-Bao (each round = 1 min; start with 1 min + 1 per life-link carried, max 5 rounds). Discovery DC 29 Willowshore Lore / DC 30 Society / DC 32 Perception. Influence skills: DC 28 Nindoru Lore, DC 30 Religion, DC 32 Society, DC 30 Diplomacy, DC 31 Intimidation, DC 33 Deception. Resistance: implying his actions harmed the town raises that DC by 2. Weakness: carrying a life-link lowers that PC's DCs by 2; giving him the Fang and Key lowers all by 2 more. Penalty: visibly carrying the Fang and Key raises that PC's DCs by 2 (until given to him).

Influence thresholds: reach 7 by the last round = he abandons Kugaptee but the two unrisen still attack (then Heh Shan-Bao Freed). Reach 10 anytime = encounter ends, unrisen vanish, he casts Kugaptee aside (Heh Shan-Bao Freed). Below 7 = he attacks. At Influence 4 the Fang-and-Key carry penalty is negated.

Defeating him in combat: at 0 HP he collapses; combat continues until the unrisen are down, then he briefly revives, shrieks, and bursts into crimson butterflies - his soul consumed by Kugaptee. Proceed to Kugaptee's Final Death.

HEH SHAN-BAO FREED: at Influence 7-9 he's freed but Kugaptee consumes his soul (no afterlife) - after thanking the PCs he bursts into butterflies in horror ('Kugaptee! He's here!'). At Influence 10 he's freed serenely ('he cannot touch my eternal soul'), restored to human form (resplendent if 10), his soul to the Boneyard for judgment. Either way Kugaptee is denied his vessel.

clusters.name: Kugaptee's Final Death (The Four-Round Cataclysm)
clusters.scene: With Heh Shan-Bao's fate resolved, Kugaptee reacts. If the PCs died/failed, his claw smashes down and he is reborn - catastrophe. Otherwise his claw is drawn back into the ground over FOUR rounds of escalating harm (tremors, butterfly-swarms, psychic anguish, the pull of death). The PCs can't escape until it ends; carrying the four life-links shields them from each stage in turn.
threads: Defeat Heh Shan-Bao / stop Kugaptee's reincarnation
clusters.gate: occurs after Heh Shan-Bao's defeat or rescue, if the PCs survived

fragments.plot_point: Round 1 The World Trembles: earthquake, 5d6 bludgeoning (DC 30 basic Reflex). Carrying the LETTER (from the Wisdom scroll) negates it for all PCs (the letter vanishes). Round 2 The Flesh Tears: razor butterflies, 5d6 slashing (DC 30 basic Fort). Carrying the OK JINJU PORTRAIT negates it (portrait vanishes).

Round 3 The Mind Recoils: telepathic anguish, 5d6 mental (DC 30 basic Will). Carrying THE WISDOM OF THE SEVEN SAGES negates it (scroll vanishes). Round 4 The Final Death: a glimpse of death, 5d6 void (DC 30 basic - choose Fort/Reflex/Will). Carrying the CAMELLIA FLOWER & RIBBON negates it (they vanish). If the PCs fail and perish, Kugaptee is reborn and Shenmen is doomed.

clusters.name: A Heroine Passes Her Burden (Tan Sui-Jing / Denouement)
clusters.scene: As long as one PC survives, the survivors huddle in a ruined Willowshore as mist rolls in and a flute plays 'The Dusklight Torch' (DC 25 Arts Lore/Performance) - a heroic-opera theme of a new generation claiming hope from a fallen predecessor. Each PC (even the dead) sees a vision of their bravery and a sunset-silhouetted swordswoman who drops her sword for them: Tan Sui-Jing (DC 20 Perception), the ancient heroine reincarnated as the sugi over Kugaptee's grave.
clusters.gate: occurs after surviving Kugaptee's Final Death

fragments.plot_point: REVELATION: the swordswoman is Tan Sui-Jing, who long ago defeated Kugaptee and was reincarnated as the sugi over his grave. She fully restores the PCs (all HP healed, all conditions removed, even the dead revived) and, in exchange, draws on their experiences and spiritual power to RESTORE the sugi tree - achieving what Heh's failed ritual sought. The PCs then awaken in the real world in the now-restored manor. Withhold her identity until the vision.

Concluding: with Kugaptee dead and the Tan Sugi restored, Willowshore's place in modern Shenmen is assured; the monastery's sugi glows silver and draws new pilgrims. If on good terms: Lo Kuon offers to rebuild the Silkwasps as Willowshore road agents; Great Willow and Isori report the natural-world omens have faded (Isori notes a few faint ones remain). Ren Mei Li keeps her word; Willowshore becomes a whispered sanctuary from the jorogumo.
